newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude eases on run cuts, technicals.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude eases on run cuts, technicals.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures eased back from early highs on Thursday after news of crude oil throughput cuts in Rotterdam and technical factors, brokers said.
June Brent, which expires at the close on Thursday, was six cents a barrel down at $19.45 at 0950 GMT while July Brent was 12 cents off at $19.42.
June gas oil stood $1.00 firmer at $171.75 after opening at $172.25.
Brokers said the weakness was partly technical, and partly a result of news that Texaco had cut crude throughputs by 20 percent at its 400,000 barrels per day (bpd) Nerefco refinery.
"It has had some effect" one broker said.
A trader familiar with the refinery's opperations said: "We are going to cut crude throughput by 10 percent overall in May, that means a 20 percent cut for the second half of the month."
Brokers said the lower Brent loading programme had not had an impact on IPE futures prices because it was more or less in line with expectations.

The June Brent loading programme released on Thursday morning was for the equivalent of 38.4 cargoes, compared to 41.8 cargoes in May. The fall partly reflected a shorter month as well as maintenance at some of the Brent system fields.
